notes: The image shows the black wire on the Pi's GND pin (physical pin 9) and the purple wire on GP17 (physical pin 11). I mapped pin 9 to GND.2, assuming GND ports are numbered in pin order (6, 9, 14, ...).

The wires are drawn with dashes running along the breadboard row from column a toward the buzzer. I read this as the buzzer legs sitting in 15t.e and 18t.e, in the same strips as the wire ends at 15t.a and 18t.a.
The buzzer is an active buzzer, so no resistor is used (the manual says so).
The manual and image give no polarity markings. I assumed buzzer port 1 is the positive leg (to GP17) and port 2 is the negative leg (to GND), as the manual says it is wired like an LED.
The wire ends are assumed: 'a' is the female end on the Pi header and 'b' is the male end in the breadboard.
The Pi is not physically placed on the breadboard. Only the jumper wires link them.
